headline: Mark Zuckerberg argues that the real AI danger is one power controlling the technology.
score_reason: Pool 7 lowered by 1: manifesto released Mon 5 Oct, before the 7 Oct window (stale).
importance_line: Meta's argument against slowing model releases affects AI users and governments deciding AI rules, and it is one company's position, not a settled policy.
summary: International Business Times reports, citing Axios and the Wall Street Journal, that Meta chief executive Mark Zuckerberg released a 6,500-word manifesto on Monday, 5 Oct 2026, arguing that the bigger AI danger is one government, company or institution controlling the technology. He argues that slowing American model releases, even by a month, would add risk while rival countries race ahead, which is widely read as a reply to the calls to slow AI development, including Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei's blog post of the week before.
notes: Stale item (event Mon 5 Oct, before 7 Oct); the summary says the date. REPLY FRAMING: the link to Amodei's post comes from ABC7 (C05-04), not from this article, so it is worded 'widely read as'. Source chain: IBTimes relays Axios and WSJ; manifesto not read directly.
